Goa Public Service Commission · CBRT for Homoeopathic Physician, Directorate of Health Services (Advt. 06/2026)

Sit a full 60-mark CBRT under exam conditions.

The CBRT is 60 marks in 75 minutes: Comprehension 10, Grammar 5, General Knowledge and Current Affairs of India and Goa 10, Logical Reasoning 10, and a 25-mark core section. All 25 sets follow this pattern and run 75 minutes. Sections I, II and IV are taken from GPSC CBRT papers of 2023 to 2026, including the medical papers; each explanation names its paper. Comprehension and grammar in Sets 1 to 12 now follow the 2026 GPSC pattern: two real GPSC passages of 2025–26 per set, and grammar items in the style of the 2026 grammar blocks. The GK section (III) of every set is written for the 1 November 2026 exam: mostly current affairs from August to October 2026, plus Goa, important days and some static GK, in the proportions GPSC has used in its recent papers. The core sections cover all ten syllabus topics: Repertory (Set 1), Anatomy and Physiology (Set 2), Pathology and Microbiology (Set 3), Practice of Medicine (Set 4), OBG, Paediatrics and Surgery (Set 5), Materia Medica and Pharmacy (Sets 6 to 8, with Organon in 8), and all ten core topics in every set from 9 to 25, with each explanation naming its topic.

Practice by level

Nine full 60-mark tests, three at each level, on the same pattern and timing as the real CBRT, with all ten core topics in each. Every question in the 25 sets was graded Easy (one-step recall of a commonly taught fact), Intermediate (a specific detail, a rule applied, or two steps of reasoning) or Hard (fine detail such as aphorism numbers or exact figures, NOT/EXCEPT and multi-statement questions, multi-step puzzles, inference beyond the passage). Each level test draws only questions of its level, topped up from the next level where the bank runs short; no question is used in two level tests. Start with Easy to build speed, then work up to Hard. Each practice set above is labelled with its overall level too.

English drills

For syllabus Sections I and II (Comprehension 10, Grammar 5): grammar in the 2026 pattern, vocabulary and usage, five real GPSC passages, and five health and medicine passages. Built from every English question in GPSC papers from 2021 to September 2026.

GK drills

Six 25-question drills, 15 minutes each, on the GK topics GPSC asks most, built from every GK question in GPSC papers from 2018 to September 2026. Current affairs run to mid-October 2026.

Where GPSC's printed answer key was wrong, the corrected answer is used and the explanation says so. In the real paper the core questions come first; here they come last, in syllabus order. Results from earlier versions of Sets 1, 2, 6, 7, 8, 9 and 12 are kept and still open for review.

  • Each question has five options. The fifth is always "None of the above", as in the real test.
  • One mark for a right answer. No marks are deducted for a wrong one.
  • Move between questions in any order from the bubble grid. Mark a question for review to come back to it.
  • The test submits itself when the clock reaches zero. Marked answers are counted.
  • After you submit you get your score, a section breakdown and every answer explained. The attempt is added to your results.

Back up and sync your progress

Download one small file with every attempt and any test in progress. Send it to yourself on WhatsApp, keep it on your phone, or upload it in the GPSCavy app or in a chat with Claude. Uploading a file adds its attempts here; nothing you already have is removed.

Qualifying marks: 30 of 60 for General, EWS and ex-servicemen, 27 for OBC, PwD and CFF, 24 for SC and ST. Candidates are then shortlisted for interview at five per post, in order of merit within each category.
